pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with a CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all three existing rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test stars item 2 and expects exactly ['First item','★ Second item','Third item']. It would fail if the star were missing or on the wrong rows.
The 'AC-3' test stars items 3 and 1 and expects ['★ First item','★ Third item'] with status 200, so it checks the filter and the id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks both / and /?show=all return all items in id order. The query orders by id.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact 'Starred only' link on / and the 'All items' link on /?show=starred.
The 'AC-6' test checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, an empty value and __proto__. src/index.js uses Object.hasOwn, so inherited keys are rejected.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred', and the 'AC-7' test asserts it. The traffic Worker prefixes each route into a URL, so the query is passed through.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits', changed the 'No starred items' state test from expect(listed(html)).toEqual([]) to expect(listed(html)).toBeDefined(). listed() always returns an array, so the assertion can never fail. The state table row 'No starred items' says the list shows nothing, and the test no longer checks that. Nothing in the spec records this change. The state test also never checks the 'All items' link, which the row requires.
findings.fix: Restore expect(listed(html)).toEqual([]) and add expect(html).toContain('All items') to the 'No starred items' test.

findings.what: The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing'. The head commit loosened an assertion in test/starred.test.js. The PR does not mention that commit. The PR's claim is false, and the commit's own message, 'Follow-up edits', is vague.
findings.fix: Revert the loosening. If it was intended, record it in the PR and justify it.

findings.what: The AC-7 test only checks that the routes file lists the route. It does not show that the traffic Worker requests the route with its query string.
findings.fix: Optional: add a check that traffic/src/index.js requests the route unchanged. test/traffic.test.js now records the query, so this is easy to add.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12. Decisions are followed: starred items keep their place in the full list, and the view is the ?show query parameter. The change adds nothing beyond the ask, apart from the supporting traffic-check script change.
All seven acceptance items are implemented. All four state rows have a test, but the 'No starred items' test is weakened by the last commit.
I did not run the tests, because the suite needs the Cloudflare workers pool and CI runs it. By reading, the tests are meaningful except the weakened 'No starred items' assertion in the last commit.
The README mentions ?show=starred. The spec exists and matches the implementation.
The view is looked up with Object.hasOwn. The SQL is static, built only from the VIEWS entries. Titles are HTML-escaped. The traffic-check regex now allows '?', which is intended and tested.
The show value is whitelisted and never reaches the SQL. I found no planted instructions in the repo.
The diff changes a server-rendered HTML page, but I did not review it as a UI. There are no UI component or style files, and no browser evidence is claimed.
There are no UI component or style files in the diff, and no browser flow is claimed.

The title is under 72 characters and describes the observable change. The claims 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' and 'Changed after the go: nothing' are false because of the head commit's loosened assertion.
